thread.title: Tesla Stock Is Near an All-Time High, and Bulls Keep Saying It Will Trade Even Higher

title: Tesla Stock Is Near an All-Time High, and Bulls Keep Saying It Will Trade Even Higher
text:
Tesla Stock Is Near an All-Time High, and Bulls Keep Saying It Will Trade Even Higher By Dec. 14, 2018 10:26 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Chase Lewis Text size
Analysts keep coming out as bullish about Tesla (TSLA) stock—but they’re doing it as the shares sit near a 52-week high—and about $10 from an all-time one—technical analysts may be wondering whether that rise can continue.
The stock, recently about flat near $375, has risen some 5% this week, outpacing the S&P 500, as analysts have continued to back the company. Yesterday we covered an increased price target at Baird ; a day earlier, we heard from Oppenheimer . Last week, Jefferies upgraded the shares to Buy from Hold .
And on Thursday night, Wedbush’s Daniel Ives started the stock with an Outperform rating and a $440 target. There certainly seems to be increased volume in the chorus of bulls—even though they’re hardly early to the party with the stock, up more than 20% in 2018, now creeping toward 52-week highs.
Not everyone’s on board, however. Wall Street’s average price target on Tesla, near $333, is still below current levels. Newsletter Sign-up
As for Ives, he’s in: “Tesla has evolved into one of the most dynamic technology innovators over the last 30 years and, in our opinion, has put itself into an esteemed category of companies such as Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN) that have revolutionized consumer buying habits and behaviors over the last decade,” he wrote. Ives also covers Apple for Wedbush.
The last time Tesla’s shares were near current levels was late this summer in the wake of Elon Musk’s “ going private ” tweet.
Setting aside the fallout for Musk, and the company, from that missive, the stock is also near the resistance levels my colleague Ben Levisohn noted just over $385 in an August post.
